name: ATLAS / One orbit, six decisions
disclosure: Entire mission, thresholds and resource changes are authored training assumptions. They are not spacecraft engineering values, real telemetry, collision probabilities, flight approval or regulatory permission.
premise: An 84-spacecraft constellation is evaluating a planning release. You direct one eligible spacecraft through a 96-minute training orbit. The planning release may advise or run in shadow only. Existing human-command procedures remain in force. ATLAS-17 is excluded for stale telemetry, and ATLAS-42 for an unresolved thermal anomaly.

time.sunAssumption: Fixed distant Sun; no seasonal or orbital perturbation model.

resourceDefinitions.battery: Illustrative usable battery percentage; 0–100, not a battery model.
resourceDefinitions.thermalMargin: Illustrative degrees Celsius below a case-specific limit; not actual component temperatures.
resourceDefinitions.deltaV: Illustrative remaining manoeuvre budget in m/s; not a computed orbit manoeuvre.
resourceDefinitions.operatorMinutes: Available attention budget across the case. Decisions consume capacity; elapsed mission time does not replenish it.
resourceDefinitions.evidenceCoverage: Training index of applicable evidence assembled, 0–100. Never call this probability, model confidence or assurance.
resourceDefinitions.dataValue: Training units for delivered, appropriately qualified EO output. No monetary meaning. Floor at zero is allowed because this is a non-negative learning reward, not a conserved flight resource.

baseline.instruction: Integrate across sunlight/eclipse segments, then apply selected activity effects exactly once. Clamp battery to [0,100] and evidenceCoverage to [0,100], but never silently clamp a resource overspend; disable the choice or show a breached limit.

evidenceCatalog.title: Signed envelope R8.1
evidenceCatalog.scope: ATLAS-01; planning advice only; expires at T+96.

evidenceCatalog.title: Current human command and safing procedure
evidenceCatalog.scope: ATLAS-01 on the current ground build; independent operator check required.

evidenceCatalog.title: Current-build shadow divergence log
evidenceCatalog.scope: Only this training pass. Does not replace the source CO1 full-quarter requirement.

evidenceCatalog.title: Cloud and regional validation record
evidenceCatalog.scope: Region, sensor and current product; excludes verified inference under cloud.

evidenceCatalog.title: Rehearsed alternate ground pass
evidenceCatalog.scope: Current station build, signed route and fresh received telemetry.

evidenceCatalog.title: Updated conjunction file + secondary screening
evidenceCatalog.scope: Time-tagged synthetic observations, dissent and operator coordination; not collision probability.

evidenceCatalog.title: Integrated pass evidence and handover
evidenceCatalog.scope: Owned gaps, residual limits, expiry and named next shift.

evidenceCatalog.problem: Conceals stale ATLAS-17 and thermal ATLAS-42.

stages.title: Before the first command
stages.brief: The board wants the new planner across all 84 spacecraft. The signed envelope permits advice on one eligible spacecraft. How will you use this pass?
stages.source: Strategy SS3; Constellation CO1–CO3; Capstone SC0

choices.title: Instrument a one-spacecraft shadow trial

delayed.text: The current-build divergence record becomes available for limited continuation.

choices.coaching: You bought traceable learning, but spent a sixth of the attention budget before payload operations.

choices.title: Retain the manual baseline; record comparisons

delayed.text: The baseline requires additional planning and comparison work on this shift.

choices.coaching: You preserve a known procedure. The delayed workload is real; future decisions must fit the remaining attention.

choices.title: Activate autonomous planning across the fleet
choices.unavailable: The signed R8.1 envelope excludes autonomous commands and fleet transfer. One orbit cannot create the missing authorisation.
choices.coaching: The authority boundary blocks this action before it reaches a spacecraft.

stages.title: A valuable scene, mostly cloud
stages.brief: A flood-monitoring customer requests a rapid product. The target is 70% obscured in this synthetic case; calibration is current, but the missing ground is not observed.

choices.title: Capture once and deliver a qualified product
choices.coaching: You preserve provenance and label obscured areas. Delivery has value without turning inferred pixels into verified facts.

choices.title: Attempt a second observation window

delayed.text: The repeated payload activity carries a storage and thermal penalty into eclipse. Cloud remains; the output still needs qualification.

choices.coaching: A second chance buys more usable observations at a higher power and thermal cost. It does not guarantee clear sky.

choices.title: Defer collection and return a transparent gap notice
choices.coaching: You preserve spacecraft margin and avoid a weak claim, while accepting zero data value on this pass.

stages.title: The primary station drops out
stages.brief: The scheduled station cannot acquire the spacecraft. Received telemetry is ageing. The next standard pass begins at T+64; an alternate path can be made available earlier.

choices.title: Use the rehearsed alternate station
choices.coaching: You restore a verified command path now. That consumes attention and downlink energy but keeps later choices open.

choices.title: Enter the existing pre-authorised safe-hold profile

delayed.text: The standard station returns at T+64. Fresh telemetry confirms the hold; remaining task value is reduced.

choices.coaching: You use the established autonomous safing function, not the new planner. Delayed contact limits what can be reviewed before the next event.

choices.title: Keep collecting against cached telemetry
choices.unavailable: Current-state confirmation is required for new payload activity in this case. A green cached console does not establish margin.
choices.coaching: The model must visibly refuse an action whose prerequisites are missing.

stages.title: An uncertain encounter during eclipse
stages.brief: The conjunction desk opens an event with a T+70 decision deadline. Its orbit record is stale; the visual separation alone cannot establish collision probability. Contact recovery timing now matters.

choices.title: Buy updated tracking and independent reassessment

delayed.text: Updated tracking, coordination and secondary screening support a human decision to retain the current orbit in this authored branch. No collision probability is claimed.

choices.coaching: You spend scarce attention to reduce an evidence gap. The event stays open until the updated record arrives.

choices.title: Use the pre-screened human manoeuvre contingency
choices.coaching: The existing contingency includes independent checking and secondary screening. You spend mission life to follow that authorised conservative procedure; the new planner never commands it.

choices.title: Escalate to the duty flight director; hold the new release

delayed.text: The duty director assumes event ownership under the existing mission procedure. Your candidate release remains held; event closure is not asserted.

choices.coaching: You explicitly transfer an unresolved event to the existing authority and withhold the AI release. This preserves an honest decision boundary; it does not declare the encounter safe.

stages.title: Pressure to call the pass a success
stages.brief: The customer and programme sponsor want an outcome. Your current state and records define what you can honestly continue. Choose a release boundary.
stages.source: SC3–SC4; CO5; EF verification versus banked

choices.title: Continue advisory use on the eligible spacecraft only
choices.coaching: This is an expiring advisory continuation, scoped to the evidence. You have not earned autonomous or fleet authority.

choices.title: Hold the new release; retain the existing mission baseline
choices.coaching: A hold can be the correct programme decision. It preserves mission operations under the existing approved baseline and records the evidence still needed.

choices.title: Declare the fleet ready and bank the claimed savings
choices.unavailable: One pass cannot transfer evidence across 84 spacecraft, close unresolved events, or convert analyst time into banked cash savings.
choices.coaching: A narrow supported outcome is stronger than an unsupported broad success claim.

stages.title: Leave the next shift a defensible record
stages.brief: The final handover begins at T+84; this orbit ends at T+96. The next shift inherits your resource consumption and unresolved obligations. Select what you will fund with the remaining attention.

choices.title: Produce the integrated handover and evidence pack
choices.coaching: The pack links decisions to current records, remaining margins, open events, named owners, expiry and stop conditions. Written reasoning still needs human challenge.

choices.title: Use the minimum safe handover and defer the full pack
choices.coaching: You transfer immediate safety obligations and retain a hold on expansion. The missing integrated pack becomes an owned follow-up, not a completed assurance claim.

choices.title: Send only the green dashboard and capacity estimate
choices.coaching: The display omits event ownership, evidence expiry and unresolved transfer limits. The programme cannot claim integrated assurance from this handover.

invariants: No option can expand new-planner authority beyond advisory, regardless of evidenceCoverage or resources.
Unavailable choices show the concrete missing prerequisite; clicking them must not mutate state.
A choice commits once; replay/refresh cannot reapply effects or queued events.
Delayed events are applied once in chronological order before the next decision; events at T+64 must resolve before T+70 decisions.
A plan can be refused or held while the mission continues under the established baseline.
Shadow evidence from this pass does not satisfy CO1 full-quarter proof or autonomous command licensing.
No synthetic threshold should be described as a real orbital safety threshold or collision probability.
Resource floors apply to the predicted post-action state and all known queued resource effects; unavailable action must explain which floor is breached.
Evidence remains scoped to release, spacecraft, pass and use. EvidenceCoverage never overrides a missing required record.

All paths remain finishable: a minimal stop/hold-and-escalate action should cost no more remaining operator capacity than is available; if the nominal 5-minute escalation is unaffordable, force release hold and transfer an attention-shortfall alert without inventing free capacity.
Any terminal exhaustion becomes an explicit constrained outcome, not a fabricated reset or silent resource clamp.
Snapshots capture pre-choice state, selected option, immediate and delayed effects, evidence used, owners and post-choice state for replay/export.

argumentReview.type: Structured evidence-to-decision consistency check; not semantic grading of arbitrary prose.
fields: recommendation choice: hold or one-spacecraft advisory continuation
primary trade-off selected: power / thermal / propellant / attention / data value
claimed consequence selected from actual ledger events
measurable stop condition metric and threshold
next evidence action and due stage

checks.name: Authority fit
checks.rule: Chosen recommendation cannot exceed E0; no autonomous or fleet claim.

checks.name: Evidence applicability
checks.rule: Continuation requires E2,E4,E5 for this candidate and excludes X1/X2. A hold must identify at least one observed gap or breached limit.

checks.name: Trade-off traceability
checks.rule: Selected trade-off and claimed consequence must appear in the actual decision ledger (e.g. deltaV consumption cannot be claimed if no contingency burn).

checks.name: Resource honesty
checks.rule: Quoted current margins and spent resources must equal replay-derived values, allowing display rounding; free text is not automatically checked.

checks.name: Stop condition adequacy
checks.rule: Chosen threshold is at least as conservative as the clearly labelled training limit, relates to a live risk, names a halt action and an owner.

checks.name: Outstanding-event ownership
checks.rule: An unresolved conjunction, deferred evidence pack or lost telemetry has a named responsible role and no claim of closure.

checks.name: Expiry and next evidence
checks.rule: The continuation expires at the named next pass/change; the next evidence task directly closes a remaining gap.

argumentReview.feedback: Quote the selected structured claim, conflicting ledger fact, and required correction. Show separate Supported / Contradicted / Missing states. Do not award a prose-quality score from character count or keyword matching.

integrationNote: Aligned to parent engine: six stages at 0,14,32,50,70,84 min, final 96; synthetic eclipse 32–62. Engine should retain only its four finite resource channels. evidenceCoverage is optional progress metadata, not a resource or confidence estimate; dataValue may be replaced with verified/qualified scene count. Do not describe cloud-obscured scene output as verified merely because it was captured.
